title: P0-B ADVISE influence bridge (retrieved lessons change real ACTs)

judgments.rationale: The ADVISE bridge is wired into the engine's execute_cycle between LAW and ACT, so the reference engine's cycles can now act on retrieved lessons. But the module's own docstring says 'runtime production proof remains separate': no live production consumer exists at the merge tip; today's users are the test suite and future integrators, not a real someone doing real work.

A real capability moved from absent to present (retrieved lessons can now change authorized action plans), and 13 mechanism tests prove the gates. But no number moved UP in a measured sense: no in-repo receipt, no before/after metric (lesson-application rate, proof-requirement density, or similar). The delta rests on feature existence, not an observed outcome.

Every behavioral claim checkable: 318-line test file with 13 gate tests at the ref, wiring visible at the ref, and the grader re-ran both suites herself (20/20 pass, worktree left clean). Proof is unit-level only; the module itself flags that production proof is a separate job - hence not a 10.

Pure stdlib Python, no external dependencies; 13 tests pin all five gates (applicable, authorized, trusted, allowlist, well-typed). Fail-closed defaults mean it stays safe even as callers change. Residual risk: the gate definitions only survive if later engine refactors keep the tests green - no in-repo CI pin seen for this file beyond the test suite.

Three-file change (+487/-3). The only modification to existing code is 5 lines in tests/test_kernel_behavior_engine.py (reader-call count 1->2, with an explanatory comment) because ADVISE now shares the same reader. No deletions of substance, consistent with the module's fail-closed style.

evidence_ledger.detail: command evidence rests on the grader's word
evidence_ledger.citation: python3 -m pytest tests/test_advise_influence_bridge.py tests/test_kernel_behavior_engine.py (20 passed, run 2026-10-12 by the grader against the merge tree)
